    // was `if (funds > 0) "solvent" else 0`: both branches must agree
    return if (funds > 0) "solvent" else "broke";
}

pub fn main() !void {
    // was `const unused = 5;` with nothing reading it
    const roles = [_]Role{ .mekwarrior, .tech, .medic };
    for (roles) |r| {
        std.debug.print("{s} earns {d}\n", .{ @tagName(r), salary(r) });
    }
    // was `const n = ...; for (...) |n|`: the capture shadowed the constant
    const n = try parse("42");
    std.debug.print("parsed {d}\n", .{n});
    _ = label(n);
    // was `const days: u8 = 365;`: u8 cannot represent 365
    const days: u16 = 365;
    std.debug.print("days in the year: {d}\n", .{days});
}

Each comment marks what was there before. The order in which the compiler reports them can vary with what it analyses first, so always fix the top one and re-run rather than trying to fix all six from one output.

Exercise 37.2 · Rename to the conventions practice

The starter is correct but named like C and Java: c_bills_t, PERSON, GetBaseSalary, HiredDay. Rename everything to Zig convention, add a /// comment to each public declaration, and run zig fmt. The tests check behaviour only, so if they still pass you have not broken anything. Name the file: exercises/37-style/ex2_naming.zig.

Solution 
//! Chapter 37, exercise 2: rename to the conventions.
//! Run with:  zig test ex2_naming.zig
//! Goal: the starter uses C-style and Java-style names. Rename every
//! identifier to Zig convention (TitleCase types, camelCase functions,
//! snake_case values) and add a doc comment to each public declaration.
//! The tests only check behaviour, so the compiler is your reviewer.

const std = @import("std");

/// Money in C-bills. Integer, always.
pub const CBills = i64;

/// A person's job in the company.
pub const Role = enum {
    mekwarrior,
    tech,

    /// Monthly pay before any modifiers.
    pub fn baseSalary(self: Role) CBills {
        return switch (self) {
            .mekwarrior => 1_500,
            .tech => 800,
        };
    }
};

/// One hired person.
pub const Person = struct {
    name: []const u8,
    role: Role,
    hired_day: u32,

    /// True once the person has served at least `min_days`.
    pub fn isVeteran(self: Person, today: u32, min_days: u32) bool {
        return today >= self.hired_day and today - self.hired_day >= min_days;
    }
};

/// Total monthly payroll for a roster.
pub fn monthlyPayroll(people: []const Person) CBills {
    var total: CBills = 0;
    for (people) |p| total += p.role.baseSalary();
    return total;
}

test "payroll adds the roster" {
    const roster = [_]Person{
        .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior, .hired_day = 0 },
        .{ .name = "Clay", .role = .tech, .hired_day = 3 },
    };
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 2_300), monthlyPayroll(&roster));
}

test "veteran after enough days" {
    const p: Person = .{ .name = "Lori", .role = .mekwarrior, .hired_day = 10 };
    try std.testing.expect(!p.isVeteran(40, 90));
    try std.testing.expect(p.isVeteran(100, 90));
}

Types became CBills, Role, Person; functions baseSalary, isVeteran, monthlyPayroll; fields hired_day. Nothing else changed, which is the point: convention is free once you know it.

Exercise 37.3 · Assert, unreachable, or error? practice

Implement four small functions, choosing for each impossible case between std.debug.assert, unreachable, an error, or nothing at all because the type already excludes it: daysInMonth(Month), discount(amount, bp) with bp promised to be 0 to 10000, parseMonth(text) from user input, and digitValue(ch) whose callers have already checked isDigit. Name the file: exercises/37-style/ex3_assert.zig.

Solution 
//! Chapter 37, exercise 3: assert, unreachable, or error?
//! Run with:  zig test ex3_assert.zig
//! Goal: implement the three functions, choosing the right tool for each
//! impossible case: `std.debug.assert` for a caller-side contract,
//! `unreachable` for a case the type system already excludes, and an
//! error for input that comes from the outside world.

const std = @import("std");

const Month = enum(u8) { jan = 1, feb, mar, apr, may, jun, jul, aug, sep, oct, nov, dec };

/// Days in a month of a non-leap year. `month` is an enum, so every case
/// is covered: no `else` and no `unreachable` needed at all.
pub fn daysInMonth(month: Month) u8 {
    return switch (month) {
        .jan, .mar, .may, .jul, .aug, .oct, .dec => 31,
        .apr, .jun, .sep, .nov => 30,
        .feb => 28,
    };
}

/// The caller promises `bp` is at most 100 percent. Breaking that promise
/// is a bug in the caller, so we assert rather than return an error.
pub fn discount(amount: i64, bp: i64) i64 {
    std.debug.assert(bp >= 0 and bp <= 10_000);
    return amount - @divTrunc(amount * bp, 10_000);
}

/// Text typed by a user is not a bug when it is wrong; it is an error.
pub fn parseMonth(text: []const u8) error{UnknownMonth}!Month {
    return std.meta.stringToEnum(Month, text) orelse error.UnknownMonth;
}

/// A digit character 0-9 to its value. Callers filter with isDigit
/// first, so anything else is unreachable.
pub fn digitValue(ch: u8) u8 {
    return switch (ch) {
        '0'...'9' => ch - '0',
        else => unreachable,
    };
}

test "days in month" {
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u8, 31), daysInMonth(.jan));
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u8, 28), daysInMonth(.feb));
}

test "discount within contract" {
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(i64, 900), discount(1000, 1_000));
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(i64, 0), discount(1000, 10_000));
}

test "parseMonth reports bad input as an error" {
    try std.testing.expectEqual(Month.sep, try parseMonth("sep"));
    try std.testing.expectError(error.UnknownMonth, parseMonth("Sept"));
}

test "digitValue" {
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u8, 7), digitValue('7'));
}

daysInMonth takes an enum, so every case is an arm and no else exists. discount asserts its precondition. parseMonth returns an error because text from a user is not a bug. digitValue uses unreachable because its contract says callers filter first. Four impossible cases, four different answers.

Exercise 37.4 · Read the panic, fix the bug challenge

The starter runs and panics. Read the trace, find the line, fix the logic (do not remove the check or switch to ReleaseFast). After the first fix it panics again with a different message. Name the file: exercises/37-style/ex4_panic.zig.

Solution 
//! Chapter 37, exercise 4: read the panic, fix the bug.
//! Run with:  zig run ex4_panic.zig
//! Goal: the starter panics with "index out of bounds" and, after you fix
//! that, with "integer overflow". Use the stack trace to find each line,
//! then fix the logic (not the safety check). Expected output:
//!   Grayson: 1500
//!   Lori: 1500
//!   Clay: 800
//!   total 3800
//!   average 1266

const std = @import("std");

const names = [_][]const u8{ "Grayson", "Lori", "Clay" };
const pay = [_]u16{ 1500, 1500, 800 };

pub fn main() void {
    // was `i <= names.len`: one past the end
    var i: usize = 0;
    while (i < names.len) : (i += 1) {
        std.debug.print("{s}: {d}\n", .{ names[i], pay[i] });
    }
    // was `var total: u16 = 0`: 1500 + 1500 + 800 overflows u16
    var total: u32 = 0;
    for (pay) |p| total += p;
    std.debug.print("total {d}\n", .{total});
    std.debug.print("average {d}\n", .{total / pay.len});
}

The first panic is index out of bounds: index 3, len 3 from a <= that should be <. The second is integer overflow from summing three u16s into a u16; the fix is a wider accumulator, not +%, because wrapping would silently give the wrong total.

Check your understanding

  1. What does the trailing comma do in zig fmt?
    AnswerA trailing comma in a list makes the formatter lay it out one element per line; without it the list is collapsed onto one line if it fits. It is the one formatting choice left to the author.
  2. Which of these is misnamed: fn ParseInt, const MaxSize = 5, const person_id: PersonId, error.notFound?
    AnswerAll but the third. Functions are camelCase (parseInt), values are snake_case (max_size), error names are TitleCase (error.NotFound).
  3. The compiler says expected type 'i32', found 'error{InvalidCharacter,Overflow}' on a line with try. What is wrong?
    AnswerThe enclosing function's return type is i32, not an error union, so try has nowhere to send the error. Change it to !i32 or use catch.
  4. In a stack trace, which frame do you look at first?
    AnswerThe topmost frame that is in a file you wrote. Frames above it in the standard library (such as callMain in start.zig) are scaffolding.
  5. What is the difference between a panic's stack trace and an error return trace?
    AnswerA stack trace shows the call chain at the moment the program stopped. An error return trace shows each try or return error.X the error passed through on its way out, from where it was created to where it went unhandled.
  6. A user types a month name that does not exist. assert, unreachable, or error?
    AnswerAn error. Bad input from outside the program is a normal condition to handle. assert and unreachable are for conditions that only a bug in your own code could produce.
  7. What does -O ReleaseFast do to an out-of-bounds index, and which mode should you ship?
    AnswerIt removes the check, so the program reads whatever memory is there: undefined behaviour with no message. Ship ReleaseSafe, which is fully optimised and keeps the checks.
What you learned.
  • zig fmt is the only style; --check for CI; the trailing comma controls one-per-line layout.
  • Names: TitleCase types and errors, camelCase functions, snake_case everything else, snake_case files. //! documents a file, /// a declaration.
  • Idioms: init/deinit, allocator first, .empty/.init, Self, defer after acquire, errdefer for partial construction, try by default, pure core with I/O at the edges.
  • Compile errors have a location, a caret and notes; fix the first one. The six common ones: unused value, shadowing, missing switch case, branch type mismatch, try without an error-union return type, comptime overflow.
  • A panic prints a message and a stack trace; look at the first frame in your own file. An error return trace shows the path an unhandled error travelled.
  • @panic for unrecoverable states, assert for caller contracts, unreachable for cases the code has already excluded, errors for anything from outside.
  • Debug and ReleaseSafe keep safety checks; ReleaseFast removes them and turns bugs into undefined behaviour. Ship ReleaseSafe; benchmark with ReleaseFast; zig build-exe -O ReleaseFast file.zig makes a binary.

38. Capstone: a mercenary ledger from scratch

In this chapter you will build a complete program, "Small Ledger", a command-line simulator of a mercenary company's payroll, in six stages. Each stage is a single file that compiles and passes its tests on its own, and each adds one layer: types, a company with commands, a ledger, a calendar tick, seeded random events, and finally an interactive loop with save and load. By the end you will have written, in about five hundred lines, a miniature of IRON LEDGER's architecture, and the next Part of this book, which reads the real game, will feel like visiting a bigger version of your own house.

38.1 What we are building, and the shape of it

Small Ledger is a program you talk to. You hire people by name and role, advance the calendar, and watch money leave on payday. Random events nudge morale, morale nudges pay, and everything can be saved to a file and loaded back. Here is a session with the finished program:

$ printf 'hire Grayson mekwarrior\nhire Clay tech\nadvance 31\nledger\nsave ledger.sav\nquit\n' | zig run ex6_repl.zig
> hired Grayson as mekwarrior (id 1)
> hired Clay as tech (id 2)
> advanced 31 days to 3025-02-01, funds 47746
> day 31  -2254  payroll  monthly payroll
balance 47746
> saved ledger.sav
> bye

(Two people whose base pay adds up to 2300 were paid 2254 because on day 15 the dice rolled a 2 and morale dropped a point. The seed is fixed, so you will get exactly these numbers.)

The architecture has one rule, borrowed directly from the game: a pure core, and I/O at the edges. The core is a Company struct and an execute(company, command) function. It never reads a file, never reads the clock, never touches stdin. It takes values and returns values or errors. Around it sits a thin edge: a parser that turns text into commands, a printer that turns results into text, and save/load functions that hold the io. The core is where all the rules live, and because it is pure, all of it is testable with zig test and no fixtures.

Each stage is exercises/38-capstone/exN_name.zig. The starters give you the tests and the skeleton; you fill in the bodies. The solutions are complete files, and each stage's solution contains the previous stage's code, so if you get stuck you can start the next stage from the solution of the one before. The table below is the map, with the IRON LEDGER file each stage corresponds to:

StageYou buildIn IRON LEDGER
1 · typesCBills, applyBp, PersonId, Role, Personsrc/domain/types.zig, src/domain/person.zig
2 · companyCompany with an arena, Command, execute, Errorsrc/sim/state.zig, src/sim/commands.zig
3 · ledgerTransaction, Ledger, postTransaction, payrollsrc/econ/finance.zig, GameState.postTreasury
4 · tickDate, Clock, advanceDay, payday on the 1stsrc/sim/clock.zig, src/sim/tick.zig
5 · eventsRng with streams, a 2d6 morale event, hash, the golden mastersrc/sim/rng.zig, src/sim/events.zig, GameState.hash
6 · repla stdin loop, a text parser, save and load with std.Iosrc/sim/cli.zig, src/main.zig, src/persist/store.zig

38.2 Stage 1: the vocabulary

Every program has a handful of types that everything else is written in terms of. Get them right first, alone, with tests, before there is any behaviour to distract you.

Money is an integer. Not a float: floats cannot represent 0.1 exactly, and a ledger that drifts by a C-bill over a thousand transactions is a ledger nobody trusts (Chapter 5). So CBills = i64, and percentages are basis points, hundredths of a percent, so that "plus 10 percent" is applyBp(x, 11_000) and stays in integer arithmetic. Identifiers are non-exhaustive enums over u32: a PersonId is a number, but the compiler will not let you pass it where a u32 or another ID type is expected (Chapter 13). Roles are an ordinary enum with a method. A person is a struct with a default for the field that starts at zero.

Write these, then make the tests pass. Notice the test for morale: a person at morale +5 earns 2 percent per point more, and the arithmetic must be exact.

Stage 1 solution: exercises/38-capstone/solutions/ex1_types.zig 
//! Chapter 38, stage 1: the vocabulary of Small Ledger.
//! Run with:  zig test ex1_types.zig
//! Goal: define CBills, applyBp, PersonId, Role with baseSalary, and
//! Person with monthlySalary, so the tests pass.

const std = @import("std");

/// All money is integer C-bills. No floats in the ledger, ever.
pub const CBills = i64;

/// Basis points: 10_000 bp is x1.0. All multipliers go through this so
/// the arithmetic is integer and reproducible.
pub const Bp = i64;

pub fn applyBp(amount: CBills, bp: Bp) CBills {
    return @divTrunc(amount * bp, 10_000);
}

/// A typed ID: impossible to mix up with a plain integer or another ID.
pub const PersonId = enum(u32) { none = 0, _ };

pub const Role = enum {
    mekwarrior,
    tech,
    medic,
    admin,

    /// Monthly base pay.
    pub fn baseSalary(self: Role) CBills {
        return switch (self) {
            .mekwarrior => 1_500,
            .tech => 800,
            .medic => 400,
            .admin => 500,
        };
    }
};

pub const Person = struct {
    id: PersonId,
    name: []const u8,
    role: Role,
    hired_day: u32,
    /// -10 (mutinous) to +10 (devoted). Each point is 2 percent of pay.
    morale: i8 = 0,

    /// Base pay adjusted by morale: +2 percent per point.
    pub fn monthlySalary(self: Person) CBills {
        const bp: Bp = 10_000 + @as(Bp, self.morale) * 200;
        return applyBp(self.role.baseSalary(), bp);
    }
};

test "basis points stay in integers" {
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 1_500), applyBp(1_500, 10_000));
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 1_650), applyBp(1_500, 11_000));
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 900), applyBp(1_500, 6_000));
}

test "typed ids are distinct values" {
    const a: PersonId = @enumFromInt(1);
    const b: PersonId = @enumFromInt(2);
    try std.testing.expect(a != b);
    try std.testing.expect(a != .none);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 2), @intFromEnum(b));
}

test "salary follows role and morale" {
    var p: Person = .{ .id = @enumFromInt(1), .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior, .hired_day = 0 };
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 1_500), p.monthlySalary());
    p.morale = 5;
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 1_650), p.monthlySalary());
    p.morale = -10;
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 1_200), p.monthlySalary());
}
$ zig test ex1_types.zig
All 3 tests passed.

Two details deserve a look. monthlySalary builds the multiplier as 10_000 + morale * 200, so morale -10 is 8000 bp (80 percent) and +10 is 12000. And the cast @as(Bp, self.morale) widens the i8 before multiplying, because i8 * 200 would overflow. This is the game's Person.monthlySalary in miniature; the real one multiplies three factors, role, experience and rank, all in basis points.

38.3 Stage 2: a Company and its commands

The state comes next. A Company owns a list of people, a running ID counter and a treasury. The question every stateful program must answer is who frees the memory, and the answer here is the same as the game's: an arena. The company creates one arena in init, every name and every list grows out of it, and deinit frees the lot in one call (Chapter 20). No per-person destructor, no double free, no forgotten free.

pub const Error = error{ UnknownPerson, EmptyName, OutOfMemory };

pub const Company = struct {
    arena: std.heap.ArenaAllocator,
    people: std.ArrayList(Person) = .empty,
    next_id: u32 = 1,
    day: u32 = 0,
    funds: CBills,

    pub const Options = struct {
        funds: CBills = 50_000,
    };

    pub fn init(gpa: std.mem.Allocator, opts: Options) Company {
        return .{
            .arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(gpa),
            .funds = opts.funds,
        };
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Company) void {
        self.arena.deinit();
    }

    /// Every allocation the company makes comes from here and dies in deinit.
    pub fn allocator(self: *Company) std.mem.Allocator {
        return self.arena.allocator();
    }

    pub fn find(self: *Company, id: PersonId) ?*Person {
        for (self.people.items) |*p| if (p.id == id) return p;
        return null;
    }

    fn today(self: *Company) u32 {
        return self.day;
    }

    pub fn hire(self: *Company, name: []const u8, role: Role) Error!PersonId {
        if (name.len == 0) return error.EmptyName;
        const id: PersonId = @enumFromInt(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        const owned = try self.allocator().dupe(u8, name);
        try self.people.append(self.allocator(), .{
            .id = id,
            .name = owned,
            .role = role,
            .hired_day = self.today(),
        });
        return id;
    }

    pub fn fire(self: *Company, id: PersonId) Error!void {
        for (self.people.items, 0..) |p, i| {
            if (p.id == id) {
                _ = self.people.orderedRemove(i);
                return;
            }
        }
        return error.UnknownPerson;
    }
};

hire copies the name into the arena with dupe. This matters: the caller's string might be a buffer that gets reused (the REPL's line buffer will be exactly that), so the company must own its copy. The test checks this by mutating the caller's buffer after hiring. fire uses orderedRemove rather than swapRemove, because the order of the roster is part of the state we will hash later, and it must not depend on deletion history.

The second half of the stage is the command layer. A command is a tagged union, one variant per thing a user can ask for; execute is one switch that dispatches to the company's methods and returns a Result or an error from a named set (Chapter 14, Chapter 16).

pub const Command = union(enum) {
    hire: struct { name: []const u8, role: Role },
    fire: PersonId,
};

pub const Result = union(enum) {
    hired: PersonId,
    fired,
};

pub fn execute(co: *Company, cmd: Command) Error!Result {
    switch (cmd) {
        .hire => |h| return .{ .hired = try co.hire(h.name, h.role) },
        .fire => |id| {
            try co.fire(id);
            return .fired;
        },
    }
}

Why the extra layer, when the REPL could call co.hire directly? Because a union of commands is data. It can be stored in an array (a script), compared, logged, replayed, sent over a wire. Stage 5's golden-master test is an array of commands run twice. The game's Command union has about forty variants and its execute is the single entry point for the TUI, the CLI and every test.

Stage 2 solution: exercises/38-capstone/solutions/ex2_company.zig 
//! Chapter 38, stage 2: a Company and its commands.
//! Run with:  zig test ex2_company.zig
//! Goal: add a Company that owns its people through an arena, and a
//! tagged-union Command with an `execute` function that returns errors.

const std = @import("std");

}

pub const PersonId = enum(u32) { none = 0, _ };

    }
};

pub const Error = error{ UnknownPerson, EmptyName, OutOfMemory };

pub const Company = struct {
    arena: std.heap.ArenaAllocator,
    people: std.ArrayList(Person) = .empty,
    next_id: u32 = 1,
    day: u32 = 0,
    funds: CBills,

    pub const Options = struct {
        funds: CBills = 50_000,
    };

    pub fn init(gpa: std.mem.Allocator, opts: Options) Company {
        return .{
            .arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(gpa),
            .funds = opts.funds,
        };
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Company) void {
        self.arena.deinit();
    }

    /// Every allocation the company makes comes from here and dies in deinit.
    pub fn allocator(self: *Company) std.mem.Allocator {
        return self.arena.allocator();
    }

    pub fn find(self: *Company, id: PersonId) ?*Person {
        for (self.people.items) |*p| if (p.id == id) return p;
        return null;
    }

    fn today(self: *Company) u32 {
        return self.day;
    }

    pub fn hire(self: *Company, name: []const u8, role: Role) Error!PersonId {
        if (name.len == 0) return error.EmptyName;
        const id: PersonId = @enumFromInt(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        const owned = try self.allocator().dupe(u8, name);
        try self.people.append(self.allocator(), .{
            .id = id,
            .name = owned,
            .role = role,
            .hired_day = self.today(),
        });
        return id;
    }

    pub fn fire(self: *Company, id: PersonId) Error!void {
        for (self.people.items, 0..) |p, i| {
            if (p.id == id) {
                _ = self.people.orderedRemove(i);
                return;
            }
        }
        return error.UnknownPerson;
    }
};

pub const Command = union(enum) {
    hire: struct { name: []const u8, role: Role },
    fire: PersonId,
};

pub const Result = union(enum) {
    hired: PersonId,
    fired,
};

pub fn execute(co: *Company, cmd: Command) Error!Result {
    switch (cmd) {
        .hire => |h| return .{ .hired = try co.hire(h.name, h.role) },
        .fire => |id| {
            try co.fire(id);
            return .fired;
        },
    }
}

test "hire gives increasing ids and copies the name" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{});
    defer co.deinit();
    var name_buf = [_]u8{ 'C', 'l', 'a', 'y' };
    const a = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = &name_buf, .role = .tech } });
    name_buf[0] = 'X'; // the company must not be looking at our buffer
    const b = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior } });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 1), @intFromEnum(a.hired));
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 2), @intFromEnum(b.hired));
    try std.testing.expectEqualStrings("Clay", co.find(a.hired).?.name);
}

test "fire removes and refuses unknown ids" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{});
    defer co.deinit();
    const r = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Lori", .role = .mekwarrior } });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 1), co.people.items.len);
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .fire = r.hired });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), co.people.items.len);
    try std.testing.expectError(error.UnknownPerson, execute(&co, .{ .fire = r.hired }));
    try std.testing.expectError(error.EmptyName, execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "", .role = .medic } }));
}
$ zig test ex2_company.zig
All 2 tests passed.

38.4 Stage 3: the ledger

Money must move in exactly one way. If funds can be changed by any line of code that feels like it, then the ledger and the balance will disagree eventually and you will not know which is right. So: a Transaction record, a Ledger that is a list of them, and one method on Company that appends a record and adjusts the balance in the same breath.

pub const Category = enum { payroll, severance, contract, event };

pub const Transaction = struct {
    day: u32,
    amount: CBills, // income +, expense -
    category: Category,
    note: []const u8 = "",
};

pub const Ledger = struct {
    transactions: std.ArrayList(Transaction) = .empty,

    pub fn post(self: *Ledger, alloc: std.mem.Allocator, txn: Transaction) !void {
        try self.transactions.append(alloc, txn);
    }

    /// Sum of every transaction: what the ledger says we have gained or lost.
    pub fn balance(self: Ledger) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.transactions.items) |t| total += t.amount;
        return total;
    }

    pub fn sumCategory(self: Ledger, cat: Category) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.transactions.items) |t| if (t.category == cat) {
            total += t.amount;
        };
        return total;
    }
};
/// The only way money moves: a ledger entry and the balance, in lockstep.
pub fn postTransaction(self: *Company, txn: Transaction) Error!void {
    try self.ledger.post(self.allocator(), txn);
    self.funds += txn.amount;
}

pub fn monthlyPayroll(self: *Company) CBills {
    var total: CBills = 0;
    for (self.people.items) |p| total += p.monthlySalary();
    return total;
}

pub fn runPayroll(self: *Company) Error!void {
    const payroll = self.monthlyPayroll();
    if (payroll == 0) return;
    try self.postTransaction(.{
        .day = self.today(),
        .amount = -payroll,
        .category = .payroll,
        .note = "monthly payroll",
    });
}

The invariant this buys is stated as a test: funds == starting_funds + ledger.balance(), always. Firing now posts a severance transaction (one month's pay) before removing the person:

pub fn fire(self: *Company, id: PersonId) Error!void {
    for (self.people.items, 0..) |p, i| {
        if (p.id == id) {
            try self.postTransaction(.{
                .day = self.today(),
                .amount = -p.monthlySalary(),
                .category = .severance,
                .note = p.name,
            });
            _ = self.people.orderedRemove(i);
            return;
        }
    }
    return error.UnknownPerson;
}

The note field holds the person's name, which lives in the arena, so the string stays valid after the person is removed from the list. That is another quiet benefit of the arena: nothing you have ever allocated goes away until the company does, so references between records are always safe.

Stage 3 solution: exercises/38-capstone/solutions/ex3_ledger.zig 
//! Chapter 38, stage 3: a ledger of transactions and payroll.
//! Run with:  zig test ex3_ledger.zig
//! Goal: add Transaction, Ledger, Company.postTransaction (the only way
//! money moves), monthlyPayroll and runPayroll; firing now posts severance.

const std = @import("std");

pub const CBills = i64;

/// Basis points: 10_000 bp is x1.0.
pub const Bp = i64;

pub fn applyBp(amount: CBills, bp: Bp) CBills {
    return @divTrunc(amount * bp, 10_000);
}

pub const PersonId = enum(u32) { none = 0, _ };

};

pub const Category = enum { payroll, severance, contract, event };

pub const Transaction = struct {

    category: Category,
    note: []const u8 = "",
};

    transactions: std.ArrayList(Transaction) = .empty,

    pub fn post(self: *Ledger, alloc: std.mem.Allocator, txn: Transaction) !void {
        try self.transactions.append(alloc, txn);
    }

    /// Sum of every transaction: what the ledger says we have gained or lost.
    pub fn balance(self: Ledger) CBills {

        return total;

        };

};

pub const Error = error{ UnknownPerson, EmptyName, OutOfMemory };

pub const Company = struct {
    arena: std.heap.ArenaAllocator,
    people: std.ArrayList(Person) = .empty,
    next_id: u32 = 1,
    day: u32 = 0,
    funds: CBills,
    starting_funds: CBills,
    ledger: Ledger = .{},

    pub const Options = struct {
        funds: CBills = 50_000,
    };

    pub fn init(gpa: std.mem.Allocator, opts: Options) Company {
        return .{
            .arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(gpa),
            .funds = opts.funds,
            .starting_funds = opts.funds,
        };
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Company) void {
        self.arena.deinit();
    }

    /// Every allocation the company makes comes from here and dies in deinit.
    pub fn allocator(self: *Company) std.mem.Allocator {
        return self.arena.allocator();
    }

    pub fn find(self: *Company, id: PersonId) ?*Person {
        for (self.people.items) |*p| if (p.id == id) return p;
        return null;
    }

    fn today(self: *Company) u32 {
        return self.day;
    }

    pub fn hire(self: *Company, name: []const u8, role: Role) Error!PersonId {
        if (name.len == 0) return error.EmptyName;
        const id: PersonId = @enumFromInt(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        const owned = try self.allocator().dupe(u8, name);
        try self.people.append(self.allocator(), .{
            .id = id,
            .name = owned,
            .role = role,
            .hired_day = self.today(),
        });
        return id;
    }

    pub fn fire(self: *Company, id: PersonId) Error!void {
        for (self.people.items, 0..) |p, i| {
            if (p.id == id) {
                try self.postTransaction(.{
                    .day = self.today(),
                    .amount = -p.monthlySalary(),
                    .category = .severance,
                    .note = p.name,
                });
                _ = self.people.orderedRemove(i);
                return;
            }
        }
        return error.UnknownPerson;
    }

    /// The only way money moves: a ledger entry and the balance, in lockstep.
    pub fn postTransaction(self: *Company, txn: Transaction) Error!void {
        try self.ledger.post(self.allocator(), txn);
        self.funds += txn.amount;
    }

    pub fn monthlyPayroll(self: *Company) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.people.items) |p| total += p.monthlySalary();
        return total;
    }

    pub fn runPayroll(self: *Company) Error!void {
        const payroll = self.monthlyPayroll();
        if (payroll == 0) return;
        try self.postTransaction(.{
            .day = self.today(),
            .amount = -payroll,
            .category = .payroll,
            .note = "monthly payroll",
        });
    }
};

pub const Command = union(enum) {
    hire: struct { name: []const u8, role: Role },
    fire: PersonId,
};

pub const Result = union(enum) {
    hired: PersonId,
    fired,
};

pub fn execute(co: *Company, cmd: Command) Error!Result {
    switch (cmd) {
        .hire => |h| return .{ .hired = try co.hire(h.name, h.role) },
        .fire => |id| {
            try co.fire(id);
            return .fired;
        },
    }
}

test "payroll is the sum of salaries and posts one transaction" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .funds = 10_000 });
    defer co.deinit();
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior } });
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Clay", .role = .tech } });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 2_300), co.monthlyPayroll());
    try co.runPayroll();
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 7_700), co.funds);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 1), co.ledger.transactions.items.len);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, -2_300), co.ledger.sumCategory(.payroll));
}

test "firing posts severance" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .funds = 10_000 });
    defer co.deinit();
    const r = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Lori", .role = .mekwarrior } });
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .fire = r.hired });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 8_500), co.funds);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, -1_500), co.ledger.sumCategory(.severance));
}

test "the ledger and the balance never disagree" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .funds = 10_000 });
    defer co.deinit();
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "A", .role = .admin } });
    try co.runPayroll();
    try co.postTransaction(.{ .day = 0, .amount = 4_000, .category = .contract, .note = "advance" });
    try co.runPayroll();
    try std.testing.expectEqual(co.funds, co.starting_funds + co.ledger.balance());
}

In the game this is GameState.postTreasury in src/sim/state.zig and the Ledger in src/econ/finance.zig. The real Transaction also carries which company, HQ and contract it belongs to, so that every report in the game (per-company profit, contract pay received, the campaign summary) is a filter over the same list.

38.5 Stage 4: the daily tick

Time moves in one place. Add the Date struct from Chapter 34 and a Clock that carries both the civil date and the integer day_index. Replace the company's bare day field with the clock, add an advance_days command, and write advanceDay, the function that does everything one day involves. For now that is: advance the clock, and if it is the first of the month, run payroll.

/// One campaign day, in a fixed order of phases.
pub fn advanceDay(co: *Company) Error!void {
    co.clock.advance();
    if (co.clock.date.isPayday()) try co.runPayroll();
}

Small as it is, this function is the most important shape in the whole program. Every future rule (supply consumption, maintenance, contract events, battles) is one more line in advanceDay, in a fixed order, and the order is part of the specification. The game's advanceDay in src/sim/tick.zig has about fifteen phases, each a function taking *GameState, and its DayPhase enum documents the order.

The tests count paydays: 31 days from January 1st is exactly one; 365 days is exactly twelve; and the company's start date is a payday that does not pay, because payroll runs after the clock advances. That last point is the kind of off-by-one a test settles once and for all.

Stage 4 solution: exercises/38-capstone/solutions/ex4_tick.zig 
//! Chapter 38, stage 4: the daily tick and payday.
//! Run with:  zig test ex4_tick.zig
//! Goal: add Date and Clock, an `advance_days` command, and `advanceDay`,
//! which runs payroll on the first of every month.

const std = @import("std");

/// All money is integer C-bills. No floats in the ledger, ever.
pub const CBills = i64;

/// Basis points: 10_000 bp is x1.0.
pub const Bp = i64;

pub fn applyBp(amount: CBills, bp: Bp) CBills {
    return @divTrunc(amount * bp, 10_000);
}

pub const PersonId = enum(u32) { none = 0, _ };

pub const Role = enum {
    mekwarrior,
    tech,
    medic,
    admin,

    pub fn baseSalary(self: Role) CBills {
        return switch (self) {
            .mekwarrior => 1_500,
            .tech => 800,
            .medic => 400,
            .admin => 500,
        };
    }
};

pub const Person = struct {
    id: PersonId,
    name: []const u8,
    role: Role,
    hired_day: u32,
    morale: i8 = 0,

    pub fn monthlySalary(self: Person) CBills {
        const bp: Bp = 10_000 + @as(Bp, self.morale) * 200;
        return applyBp(self.role.baseSalary(), bp);
    }
};

pub const Category = enum { payroll, severance, contract, event };

pub const Transaction = struct {
    day: u32,
    amount: CBills, // income +, expense -
    category: Category,
    note: []const u8 = "",
};

pub const Ledger = struct {
    transactions: std.ArrayList(Transaction) = .empty,

    pub fn post(self: *Ledger, alloc: std.mem.Allocator, txn: Transaction) !void {
        try self.transactions.append(alloc, txn);
    }

    /// Sum of every transaction: what the ledger says we have gained or lost.
    pub fn balance(self: Ledger) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.transactions.items) |t| total += t.amount;
        return total;
    }

    pub fn sumCategory(self: Ledger, cat: Category) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.transactions.items) |t| if (t.category == cat) {
            total += t.amount;
        };
        return total;
    }
};

/// Proleptic Gregorian date, as the game uses in 3025.
pub const Date = struct {
    year: u16,
    month: u8,
    day: u8,

    pub const campaign_start: Date = .{ .year = 3025, .month = 1, .day = 1 };

    pub fn isLeapYear(year: u16) bool {
        return (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0) or year % 400 == 0;
    }

    pub fn daysInMonth(year: u16, month: u8) u8 {
        return switch (month) {
            1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12 => 31,
            4, 6, 9, 11 => 30,
            2 => if (isLeapYear(year)) @as(u8, 29) else 28,
            else => unreachable,
        };
    }

    pub fn next(self: Date) Date {
        var d = self;
        d.day += 1;
        if (d.day > daysInMonth(d.year, d.month)) {
            d.day = 1;
            d.month += 1;
            if (d.month > 12) {
                d.month = 1;
                d.year += 1;
            }
        }
        return d;
    }

    pub fn isPayday(self: Date) bool {
        return self.day == 1;
    }
};

pub const Clock = struct {
    date: Date = Date.campaign_start,
    day_index: u32 = 0,

    pub fn advance(self: *Clock) void {
        self.date = self.date.next();
        self.day_index += 1;
    }
};

pub const Error = error{ UnknownPerson, EmptyName, OutOfMemory };

pub const Company = struct {
    arena: std.heap.ArenaAllocator,
    people: std.ArrayList(Person) = .empty,
    next_id: u32 = 1,
    funds: CBills,
    starting_funds: CBills,
    ledger: Ledger = .{},
    clock: Clock = .{},

    pub const Options = struct {
        funds: CBills = 50_000,
    };

    pub fn init(gpa: std.mem.Allocator, opts: Options) Company {
        return .{
            .arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(gpa),
            .funds = opts.funds,
            .starting_funds = opts.funds,
        };
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Company) void {
        self.arena.deinit();
    }

    /// Every allocation the company makes comes from here and dies in deinit.
    pub fn allocator(self: *Company) std.mem.Allocator {
        return self.arena.allocator();
    }

    pub fn find(self: *Company, id: PersonId) ?*Person {
        for (self.people.items) |*p| if (p.id == id) return p;
        return null;
    }

    fn today(self: *Company) u32 {
        return self.clock.day_index;
    }

    pub fn hire(self: *Company, name: []const u8, role: Role) Error!PersonId {
        if (name.len == 0) return error.EmptyName;
        const id: PersonId = @enumFromInt(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        const owned = try self.allocator().dupe(u8, name);
        try self.people.append(self.allocator(), .{
            .id = id,
            .name = owned,
            .role = role,
            .hired_day = self.today(),
        });
        return id;
    }

    pub fn fire(self: *Company, id: PersonId) Error!void {
        for (self.people.items, 0..) |p, i| {
            if (p.id == id) {
                try self.postTransaction(.{
                    .day = self.today(),
                    .amount = -p.monthlySalary(),
                    .category = .severance,
                    .note = p.name,
                });
                _ = self.people.orderedRemove(i);
                return;
            }
        }
        return error.UnknownPerson;
    }

    /// The only way money moves: a ledger entry and the balance, in lockstep.
    pub fn postTransaction(self: *Company, txn: Transaction) Error!void {
        try self.ledger.post(self.allocator(), txn);
        self.funds += txn.amount;
    }

    pub fn monthlyPayroll(self: *Company) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.people.items) |p| total += p.monthlySalary();
        return total;
    }

    pub fn runPayroll(self: *Company) Error!void {
        const payroll = self.monthlyPayroll();
        if (payroll == 0) return;
        try self.postTransaction(.{
            .day = self.today(),
            .amount = -payroll,
            .category = .payroll,
            .note = "monthly payroll",
        });
    }
};

pub const Command = union(enum) {
    hire: struct { name: []const u8, role: Role },
    fire: PersonId,
    advance_days: u32,
};

pub const Result = union(enum) {
    hired: PersonId,
    fired,
    advanced: u32,
};

pub fn execute(co: *Company, cmd: Command) Error!Result {
    switch (cmd) {
        .hire => |h| return .{ .hired = try co.hire(h.name, h.role) },
        .fire => |id| {
            try co.fire(id);
            return .fired;
        },
        .advance_days => |n| {
            for (0..n) |_| try advanceDay(co);
            return .{ .advanced = n };
        },
    }
}

/// One campaign day, in a fixed order of phases.
pub fn advanceDay(co: *Company) Error!void {
    co.clock.advance();
    if (co.clock.date.isPayday()) try co.runPayroll();
}

test "31 days from January 1st crosses exactly one payday" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .funds = 10_000 });
    defer co.deinit();
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior } });
    const r = try execute(&co, .{ .advance_days = 31 });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 31), r.advanced);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(Date{ .year = 3025, .month = 2, .day = 1 }, co.clock.date);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 8_500), co.funds);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 31), co.ledger.transactions.items[0].day);
}

test "a year has twelve paydays" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .funds = 100_000 });
    defer co.deinit();
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Clay", .role = .tech } });
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .advance_days = 365 });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(Date{ .year = 3026, .month = 1, .day = 1 }, co.clock.date);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 12), co.ledger.transactions.items.len);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(CBills, 100_000 - 12 * 800), co.funds);
}

test "hired_day records the clock" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{});
    defer co.deinit();
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .advance_days = 10 });
    const r = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Lori", .role = .mekwarrior } });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 10), co.find(r.hired).?.hired_day);
}

38.6 Stage 5: dice, and the golden master

Now the simulation gets a random element, and with it the discipline that keeps randomness from ruining testability. The company gets a seed in its Options, an Rng with named streams (the miniature you built in Exercise 34.5), and a log. advanceDay gains an events phase before finances:

/// One campaign day, in a fixed order of phases: events, then finances.
pub fn advanceDay(co: *Company) Error!void {
    co.clock.advance();
    try runEvents(co);
    if (co.clock.date.isPayday()) try co.runPayroll();
}

/// The morale event: 2d6 on the events stream every day. Snake eyes and
/// boxcars are the only rolls that do anything, so most days are quiet.
fn runEvents(co: *Company) Error!void {
    const roll = co.rng.roll2d6(.events);
    switch (roll) {
        2 => {
            for (co.people.items) |*p| p.morale = @max(p.morale - 1, -10);
            try co.logf("day {d}: grumbling in the barracks (rolled 2), morale -1", .{co.clock.day_index});
        },
        12 => {
            for (co.people.items) |*p| p.morale = @min(p.morale + 1, 10);
            try co.logf("day {d}: a good day (rolled 12), morale +1", .{co.clock.day_index});
        },
        else => {},
    }
}

Every day rolls 2d6 on the .events stream. A 2 lowers everyone's morale by a point, a 12 raises it, anything else is a quiet day, so roughly one day in eighteen something happens. Morale is clamped with @max and @min. The log is a list of strings in the arena, built with allocPrint.

Then the test that makes the whole design pay off. A hash method folds the state that matters (the day, the funds, every person's ID, name, morale and hire date, and the number of transactions) into one 64-bit number with std.hash.Wyhash:

/// A 64-bit fingerprint of everything that matters. Two companies with
/// the same seed and the same commands must produce the same hash.
pub fn hash(self: *Company) u64 {
    var h = std.hash.Wyhash.init(0);
    h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&self.clock.day_index));
    h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&self.funds));
    for (self.people.items) |p| {
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.id));
        h.update(p.name);
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.morale));
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.hired_day));
    }
    const n: u64 = self.ledger.transactions.items.len;
    h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&n));
    return h.final();
}

And the golden master runs the same six commands on two fresh companies with the same seed and demands the same hash. It is a near-verbatim copy of the game's test in src/sim/commands.zig.

test "golden master: same seed + same script = same hash" {
    const script = [_]Command{
        .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior } },
        .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Lori", .role = .mekwarrior } },
        .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Clay", .role = .tech } },
        .{ .advance_days = 45 },
        .{ .fire = @enumFromInt(2) },
        .{ .advance_days = 45 },
    };
    var hashes: [2]u64 = undefined;
    for (&hashes) |*out| {
        var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .seed = 42 });
        defer co.deinit();
        for (script) |cmd| _ = try execute(&co, cmd);
        out.* = co.hash();
    }
    try std.testing.expectEqual(hashes[0], hashes[1]);
}

What this test catches: any read of the real clock, any use of an OS-seeded generator, any iteration over an unordered hash map, any thread, any uninitialised memory that leaks into the state. What it costs: a few microseconds per build. Two companion tests check that a different seed gives a different history (so the hash is not trivially constant) and that morale stays in range over two thousand days.

pub const Stream = enum(u8) {
    events,
    market,

    const count = @typeInfo(Stream).@"enum".fields.len;
};

/// One generator per subsystem, all derived from a single seed.
pub const Rng = struct {
    prngs: [Stream.count]std.Random.DefaultPrng,

    pub fn init(seed: u64) Rng {
        var self: Rng = undefined;
        for (&self.prngs, 0..) |*prng, i| {
            prng.* = std.Random.DefaultPrng.init(seed ^ (0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 *% (i + 1)));
        }
        return self;
    }

    pub fn roll2d6(self: *Rng, stream: Stream) u8 {
        const r = self.prngs[@intFromEnum(stream)].random();
        return r.intRangeAtMost(u8, 1, 6) + r.intRangeAtMost(u8, 1, 6);
    }
};

    /// A 64-bit fingerprint of everything that matters. Two companies with
    /// the same seed and the same commands must produce the same hash.
    pub fn hash(self: *Company) u64 {
        var h = std.hash.Wyhash.init(0);
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&self.clock.day_index));
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&self.funds));
        for (self.people.items) |p| {
            h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.id));
            h.update(p.name);
            h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.morale));
            h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.hired_day));
        }
        const n: u64 = self.ledger.transactions.items.len;
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&n));
        return h.final();
    }
};

pub const Command = union(enum) {
    hire: struct { name: []const u8, role: Role },
    fire: PersonId,
    advance_days: u32,
};

pub const Result = union(enum) {
    hired: PersonId,
    fired,
    advanced: u32,
};

pub fn execute(co: *Company, cmd: Command) Error!Result {
    switch (cmd) {
        .hire => |h| return .{ .hired = try co.hire(h.name, h.role) },
        .fire => |id| {
            try co.fire(id);
            return .fired;
        },
        .advance_days => |n| {
            for (0..n) |_| try advanceDay(co);
            return .{ .advanced = n };
        },
    }
}

/// One campaign day, in a fixed order of phases: events, then finances.
pub fn advanceDay(co: *Company) Error!void {
    co.clock.advance();
    try runEvents(co);
    if (co.clock.date.isPayday()) try co.runPayroll();
}

/// The morale event: 2d6 on the events stream every day. Snake eyes and
/// boxcars are the only rolls that do anything, so most days are quiet.
fn runEvents(co: *Company) Error!void {
    const roll = co.rng.roll2d6(.events);
    switch (roll) {
        2 => {
            for (co.people.items) |*p| p.morale = @max(p.morale - 1, -10);
            try co.logf("day {d}: grumbling in the barracks (rolled 2), morale -1", .{co.clock.day_index});
        },
        12 => {
            for (co.people.items) |*p| p.morale = @min(p.morale + 1, 10);
            try co.logf("day {d}: a good day (rolled 12), morale +1", .{co.clock.day_index});
        },
        else => {},
    }
}

test "golden master: same seed + same script = same hash" {
    const script = [_]Command{
        .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior } },
        .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Lori", .role = .mekwarrior } },
        .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Clay", .role = .tech } },
        .{ .advance_days = 45 },
        .{ .fire = @enumFromInt(2) },
        .{ .advance_days = 45 },
    };
    var hashes: [2]u64 = undefined;
    for (&hashes) |*out| {
        var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .seed = 42 });
        defer co.deinit();
        for (script) |cmd| _ = try execute(&co, cmd);
        out.* = co.hash();
    }
    try std.testing.expectEqual(hashes[0], hashes[1]);
}

test "a different seed gives a different history" {
    var a = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .seed = 1 });
    defer a.deinit();
    var b = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .seed = 2 });
    defer b.deinit();
    for ([_]*Company{ &a, &b }) |co| {
        _ = try execute(co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior } });
        _ = try execute(co, .{ .advance_days = 400 });
    }
    try std.testing.expect(a.hash() != b.hash());
    try std.testing.expect(a.log.items.len > 0);
}

test "morale stays within -10..10 and moves pay" {
    var co = Company.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .seed = 7, .funds = 1_000_000 });
    defer co.deinit();
    const r = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Clay", .role = .tech } });
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .advance_days = 2000 });
    const p = co.find(r.hired).?;
    try std.testing.expect(p.morale >= -10 and p.morale <= 10);
    const expected = applyBp(800, 10_000 + @as(Bp, p.morale) * 200);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(expected, p.monthlySalary());
}
$ zig test ex5_events.zig
All 3 tests passed.

38.7 Stage 6: the edge

Everything so far is pure. The last stage adds the parts that touch the world, and keeps them below a line in the file that says so:

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
// Everything above this line is the pure core: no io, no stdin, no files.
// Everything below is the edge: parsing text, printing, saving, loading.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------

const ParseError = error{ UnknownVerb, MissingArgument, BadNumber, BadRole };

const ReplCommand = union(enum) {
    sim: Command,
    people,
    ledger,
    log,
    save: []const u8,
    load: []const u8,
    quit,
};

There are two kinds of command now. Command from the core (hire, fire, advance_days) changes the simulation. ReplCommand wraps it and adds the verbs that belong only to the interactive session: printing the roster, the ledger or the log, saving, loading, quitting. Keeping them separate means the core never learns what "save" is, which is exactly right: saving is a property of this front end, not of the company.

Parsing. parseLine tokenises on spaces, matches the verb, and converts arguments with std.meta.stringToEnum (for roles) and std.fmt.parseInt (for numbers). Each failure is a named error, and the REPL prints the error's name. Note that the hire variant holds a slice into the line buffer; that is fine, because execute copies the name into the arena immediately, and the buffer is only reused on the next iteration.

fn parseLine(line: []const u8) ParseError!ReplCommand {
    var it = std.mem.tokenizeScalar(u8, line, ' ');
    const verb = it.next() orelse return error.UnknownVerb;
    if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "hire")) {
        const name = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const role_text = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const role = std.meta.stringToEnum(Role, role_text) orelse return error.BadRole;
        return .{ .sim = .{ .hire = .{ .name = name, .role = role } } };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "fire")) {
        const id_text = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const id = std.fmt.parseInt(u32, id_text, 10) catch return error.BadNumber;
        return .{ .sim = .{ .fire = @enumFromInt(id) } };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "advance")) {
        const n_text = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const n = std.fmt.parseInt(u32, n_text, 10) catch return error.BadNumber;
        return .{ .sim = .{ .advance_days = n } };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "people")) {
        return .people;
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "ledger")) {
        return .ledger;
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "log")) {
        return .log;
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "save")) {
        return .{ .save = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "load")) {
        return .{ .load = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "quit")) {
        return .quit;
    }
    return error.UnknownVerb;
}

The loop. main owns the io, the allocator, a buffered stdout writer and a buffered stdin reader (Chapter 32). It reads a line with takeDelimiter('\n'), which returns null at end of input so a piped script ends cleanly, trims it, parses, executes, prints. Every branch that can fail prints and continues; nothing a user types can crash the program.

pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void {
    const io = init.io;
    const gpa = init.gpa;
    var out_buf: [4096]u8 = undefined;
    var stdout = std.Io.File.stdout().writer(io, &out_buf);
    const out = &stdout.interface;
    var in_buf: [1024]u8 = undefined;
    var stdin = std.Io.File.stdin().reader(io, &in_buf);

    var co = Company.init(gpa, .{});
    defer co.deinit();

    while (true) {
        try out.flush();
        const raw = try stdin.interface.takeDelimiter('\n') orelse break;
        const line = std.mem.trim(u8, raw, " \t\r\n");
        if (line.len == 0) continue;
        const cmd = parseLine(line) catch |e| {
            try out.print("> error: {s}\n", .{@errorName(e)});
            continue;
        };
        switch (cmd) {
            .sim => |c| {
                const result = execute(&co, c) catch |e| {
                    try out.print("> error: {s}\n", .{@errorName(e)});
                    continue;
                };

Saving and loading. The save format is deliberately boring: one record per line, fields separated by spaces, the free-text note last so it may contain spaces. It saves the seed, the clock, the funds, the ID counter, the four words of state inside each random stream, every person, every transaction and every log line. save takes an io and a *Company and writes with a buffered file writer (Chapter 33). load reads the whole file with readFileAlloc, splits it into lines, and rebuilds a company record by record, with errdefer co.deinit() so a malformed file does not leak the half-built arena.

fn save(io: std.Io, co: *Company, path: []const u8) !void {
    var file = try std.Io.Dir.cwd().createFile(io, path, .{});
    defer file.close(io);
    var buf: [4096]u8 = undefined;
    var fw = file.writer(io, &buf);
    const w = &fw.interface;
    try w.print("smallledger 1\n", .{});
    try w.print("seed {d}\n", .{co.seed});
    try w.print("clock {d} {d} {d} {d}\n", .{ co.clock.day_index, co.clock.date.year, co.clock.date.month, co.clock.date.day });
    try w.print("funds {d} {d} {d}\n", .{ co.funds, co.starting_funds, co.next_id });
    for (co.rng.prngs, 0..) |prng, i| {
        try w.print("rng {d} {d} {d} {d} {d}\n", .{ i, prng.s[0], prng.s[1], prng.s[2], prng.s[3] });
    }
    for (co.people.items) |p| {
        try w.print("person {d} {s} {s} {d} {d}\n", .{ @intFromEnum(p.id), p.name, @tagName(p.role), p.hired_day, p.morale });
    }
    for (co.ledger.transactions.items) |t| {
        try w.print("txn {d} {d} {s} {s}\n", .{ t.day, t.amount, @tagName(t.category), t.note });
    }
    for (co.log.items) |line| try w.print("log {s}\n", .{line});
    try w.flush();
}

const LoadError = error{ BadFormat, OutOfMemory };

Saving the random streams' internal state (prng.s, four u64s each) is what makes a loaded game continue identically to the unsaved one, and the file's test proves it: save, load, advance both companies a hundred days, compare hashes. In the REPL, load replaces the running company, so its deinit is called first:

            .load => |path| {
                const loaded = load(io, gpa, path) catch |e| {
                    try out.print("> load failed: {s}\n", .{@errorName(e)});
                    continue;
                };
                co.deinit();
                co = loaded;
                try out.print("> loaded {s}: day {d}, {d} people, funds {d}\n", .{ path, co.clock.day_index, co.people.items.len, co.funds });
            },
            .quit => break,
        }
    }
    try out.print("> bye\n", .{});
    try out.flush();
}
Stage 6 solution: exercises/38-capstone/solutions/ex6_repl.zig 
//! Chapter 38, stage 6: the REPL, with save and load.
//! Run with:  printf 'hire Grayson mekwarrior\nhire Clay tech\nadvance 31\nledger\nsave ledger.sav\nquit\n' | zig run ex6_repl.zig
//! Goal: read commands from stdin, run them through the pure core, print
//! results, and persist the whole company to a text file with std.Io.
//! Verbs: hire NAME ROLE, fire ID, advance N, people, ledger, log,
//! save FILE, load FILE, quit. Expected output for the command above:
//!   > hired Grayson as mekwarrior (id 1)
//!   > hired Clay as tech (id 2)
//!   > advanced 31 days to 3025-02-01, funds 47746
//!   > day 31  -2254  payroll  monthly payroll
//!   balance 47746
//!   > saved ledger.sav
//!   > bye

const std = @import("std");

/// All money is integer C-bills. No floats in the ledger, ever.
pub const CBills = i64;

/// Basis points: 10_000 bp is x1.0.
pub const Bp = i64;

pub fn applyBp(amount: CBills, bp: Bp) CBills {
    return @divTrunc(amount * bp, 10_000);
}

pub const PersonId = enum(u32) { none = 0, _ };

pub const Role = enum {
    mekwarrior,
    tech,
    medic,
    admin,

    pub fn baseSalary(self: Role) CBills {
        return switch (self) {
            .mekwarrior => 1_500,
            .tech => 800,
            .medic => 400,
            .admin => 500,
        };
    }
};

pub const Person = struct {
    id: PersonId,
    name: []const u8,
    role: Role,
    hired_day: u32,
    morale: i8 = 0,

    pub fn monthlySalary(self: Person) CBills {
        const bp: Bp = 10_000 + @as(Bp, self.morale) * 200;
        return applyBp(self.role.baseSalary(), bp);
    }
};

pub const Category = enum { payroll, severance, contract, event };

pub const Transaction = struct {
    day: u32,
    amount: CBills, // income +, expense -
    category: Category,
    note: []const u8 = "",
};

pub const Ledger = struct {
    transactions: std.ArrayList(Transaction) = .empty,

    pub fn post(self: *Ledger, alloc: std.mem.Allocator, txn: Transaction) !void {
        try self.transactions.append(alloc, txn);
    }

    /// Sum of every transaction: what the ledger says we have gained or lost.
    pub fn balance(self: Ledger) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.transactions.items) |t| total += t.amount;
        return total;
    }

    pub fn sumCategory(self: Ledger, cat: Category) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.transactions.items) |t| if (t.category == cat) {
            total += t.amount;
        };
        return total;
    }
};

/// Proleptic Gregorian date, as the game uses in 3025.
pub const Date = struct {
    year: u16,
    month: u8,
    day: u8,

    pub const campaign_start: Date = .{ .year = 3025, .month = 1, .day = 1 };

    pub fn isLeapYear(year: u16) bool {
        return (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0) or year % 400 == 0;
    }

    pub fn daysInMonth(year: u16, month: u8) u8 {
        return switch (month) {
            1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12 => 31,
            4, 6, 9, 11 => 30,
            2 => if (isLeapYear(year)) @as(u8, 29) else 28,
            else => unreachable,
        };
    }

    pub fn next(self: Date) Date {
        var d = self;
        d.day += 1;
        if (d.day > daysInMonth(d.year, d.month)) {
            d.day = 1;
            d.month += 1;
            if (d.month > 12) {
                d.month = 1;
                d.year += 1;
            }
        }
        return d;
    }

    pub fn isPayday(self: Date) bool {
        return self.day == 1;
    }
};

pub const Clock = struct {
    date: Date = Date.campaign_start,
    day_index: u32 = 0,

    pub fn advance(self: *Clock) void {
        self.date = self.date.next();
        self.day_index += 1;
    }
};

pub const Stream = enum(u8) {
    events,
    market,

    const count = @typeInfo(Stream).@"enum".fields.len;
};

/// One generator per subsystem, all derived from a single seed.
pub const Rng = struct {
    prngs: [Stream.count]std.Random.DefaultPrng,

    pub fn init(seed: u64) Rng {
        var self: Rng = undefined;
        for (&self.prngs, 0..) |*prng, i| {
            prng.* = std.Random.DefaultPrng.init(seed ^ (0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 *% (i + 1)));
        }
        return self;
    }

    pub fn roll2d6(self: *Rng, stream: Stream) u8 {
        const r = self.prngs[@intFromEnum(stream)].random();
        return r.intRangeAtMost(u8, 1, 6) + r.intRangeAtMost(u8, 1, 6);
    }
};

pub const Error = error{ UnknownPerson, EmptyName, OutOfMemory };

pub const Company = struct {
    arena: std.heap.ArenaAllocator,
    people: std.ArrayList(Person) = .empty,
    next_id: u32 = 1,
    funds: CBills,
    starting_funds: CBills,
    ledger: Ledger = .{},
    clock: Clock = .{},
    seed: u64,
    rng: Rng,
    log: std.ArrayList([]const u8) = .empty,

    pub const Options = struct {
        funds: CBills = 50_000,
        seed: u64 = 3025,
    };

    pub fn init(gpa: std.mem.Allocator, opts: Options) Company {
        return .{
            .arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(gpa),
            .funds = opts.funds,
            .starting_funds = opts.funds,
            .seed = opts.seed,
            .rng = Rng.init(opts.seed),
        };
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Company) void {
        self.arena.deinit();
    }

    /// Every allocation the company makes comes from here and dies in deinit.
    pub fn allocator(self: *Company) std.mem.Allocator {
        return self.arena.allocator();
    }

    pub fn find(self: *Company, id: PersonId) ?*Person {
        for (self.people.items) |*p| if (p.id == id) return p;
        return null;
    }

    fn today(self: *Company) u32 {
        return self.clock.day_index;
    }

    pub fn hire(self: *Company, name: []const u8, role: Role) Error!PersonId {
        if (name.len == 0) return error.EmptyName;
        const id: PersonId = @enumFromInt(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        const owned = try self.allocator().dupe(u8, name);
        try self.people.append(self.allocator(), .{
            .id = id,
            .name = owned,
            .role = role,
            .hired_day = self.today(),
        });
        return id;
    }

    pub fn fire(self: *Company, id: PersonId) Error!void {
        for (self.people.items, 0..) |p, i| {
            if (p.id == id) {
                try self.postTransaction(.{
                    .day = self.today(),
                    .amount = -p.monthlySalary(),
                    .category = .severance,
                    .note = p.name,
                });
                _ = self.people.orderedRemove(i);
                return;
            }
        }
        return error.UnknownPerson;
    }

    /// The only way money moves: a ledger entry and the balance, in lockstep.
    pub fn postTransaction(self: *Company, txn: Transaction) Error!void {
        try self.ledger.post(self.allocator(), txn);
        self.funds += txn.amount;
    }

    pub fn monthlyPayroll(self: *Company) CBills {
        var total: CBills = 0;
        for (self.people.items) |p| total += p.monthlySalary();
        return total;
    }

    pub fn runPayroll(self: *Company) Error!void {
        const payroll = self.monthlyPayroll();
        if (payroll == 0) return;
        try self.postTransaction(.{
            .day = self.today(),
            .amount = -payroll,
            .category = .payroll,
            .note = "monthly payroll",
        });
    }

    pub fn logf(self: *Company, comptime fmt: []const u8, args: anytype) Error!void {
        const line = try std.fmt.allocPrint(self.allocator(), fmt, args);
        try self.log.append(self.allocator(), line);
    }

    /// A 64-bit fingerprint of everything that matters. Two companies with
    /// the same seed and the same commands must produce the same hash.
    pub fn hash(self: *Company) u64 {
        var h = std.hash.Wyhash.init(0);
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&self.clock.day_index));
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&self.funds));
        for (self.people.items) |p| {
            h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.id));
            h.update(p.name);
            h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.morale));
            h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&p.hired_day));
        }
        const n: u64 = self.ledger.transactions.items.len;
        h.update(std.mem.asBytes(&n));
        return h.final();
    }
};

pub const Command = union(enum) {
    hire: struct { name: []const u8, role: Role },
    fire: PersonId,
    advance_days: u32,
};

pub const Result = union(enum) {
    hired: PersonId,
    fired,
    advanced: u32,
};

pub fn execute(co: *Company, cmd: Command) Error!Result {
    switch (cmd) {
        .hire => |h| return .{ .hired = try co.hire(h.name, h.role) },
        .fire => |id| {
            try co.fire(id);
            return .fired;
        },
        .advance_days => |n| {
            for (0..n) |_| try advanceDay(co);
            return .{ .advanced = n };
        },
    }
}

/// One campaign day, in a fixed order of phases: events, then finances.
pub fn advanceDay(co: *Company) Error!void {
    co.clock.advance();
    try runEvents(co);
    if (co.clock.date.isPayday()) try co.runPayroll();
}

/// The morale event: 2d6 on the events stream every day. Snake eyes and
/// boxcars are the only rolls that do anything, so most days are quiet.
fn runEvents(co: *Company) Error!void {
    const roll = co.rng.roll2d6(.events);
    switch (roll) {
        2 => {
            for (co.people.items) |*p| p.morale = @max(p.morale - 1, -10);
            try co.logf("day {d}: grumbling in the barracks (rolled 2), morale -1", .{co.clock.day_index});
        },
        12 => {
            for (co.people.items) |*p| p.morale = @min(p.morale + 1, 10);
            try co.logf("day {d}: a good day (rolled 12), morale +1", .{co.clock.day_index});
        },
        else => {},
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
// Everything above this line is the pure core: no io, no stdin, no files.
// Everything below is the edge: parsing text, printing, saving, loading.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------

const ParseError = error{ UnknownVerb, MissingArgument, BadNumber, BadRole };

const ReplCommand = union(enum) {
    sim: Command,
    people,
    ledger,
    log,
    save: []const u8,
    load: []const u8,
    quit,
};

fn parseLine(line: []const u8) ParseError!ReplCommand {
    var it = std.mem.tokenizeScalar(u8, line, ' ');
    const verb = it.next() orelse return error.UnknownVerb;
    if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "hire")) {
        const name = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const role_text = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const role = std.meta.stringToEnum(Role, role_text) orelse return error.BadRole;
        return .{ .sim = .{ .hire = .{ .name = name, .role = role } } };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "fire")) {
        const id_text = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const id = std.fmt.parseInt(u32, id_text, 10) catch return error.BadNumber;
        return .{ .sim = .{ .fire = @enumFromInt(id) } };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "advance")) {
        const n_text = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument;
        const n = std.fmt.parseInt(u32, n_text, 10) catch return error.BadNumber;
        return .{ .sim = .{ .advance_days = n } };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "people")) {
        return .people;
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "ledger")) {
        return .ledger;
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "log")) {
        return .log;
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "save")) {
        return .{ .save = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "load")) {
        return .{ .load = it.next() orelse return error.MissingArgument };
    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, verb, "quit")) {
        return .quit;
    }
    return error.UnknownVerb;
}

/// Save format: one record per line, whitespace separated, notes last.
fn save(io: std.Io, co: *Company, path: []const u8) !void {
    var file = try std.Io.Dir.cwd().createFile(io, path, .{});
    defer file.close(io);
    var buf: [4096]u8 = undefined;
    var fw = file.writer(io, &buf);
    const w = &fw.interface;
    try w.print("smallledger 1\n", .{});
    try w.print("seed {d}\n", .{co.seed});
    try w.print("clock {d} {d} {d} {d}\n", .{ co.clock.day_index, co.clock.date.year, co.clock.date.month, co.clock.date.day });
    try w.print("funds {d} {d} {d}\n", .{ co.funds, co.starting_funds, co.next_id });
    for (co.rng.prngs, 0..) |prng, i| {
        try w.print("rng {d} {d} {d} {d} {d}\n", .{ i, prng.s[0], prng.s[1], prng.s[2], prng.s[3] });
    }
    for (co.people.items) |p| {
        try w.print("person {d} {s} {s} {d} {d}\n", .{ @intFromEnum(p.id), p.name, @tagName(p.role), p.hired_day, p.morale });
    }
    for (co.ledger.transactions.items) |t| {
        try w.print("txn {d} {d} {s} {s}\n", .{ t.day, t.amount, @tagName(t.category), t.note });
    }
    for (co.log.items) |line| try w.print("log {s}\n", .{line});
    try w.flush();
}

const LoadError = error{ BadFormat, OutOfMemory };

fn load(io: std.Io, gpa: std.mem.Allocator, path: []const u8) !Company {
    const text = try std.Io.Dir.cwd().readFileAlloc(io, path, gpa, .limited(1 << 24));
    defer gpa.free(text);

    var co = Company.init(gpa, .{});
    errdefer co.deinit();
    var lines = std.mem.splitScalar(u8, text, '\n');
    const header = lines.next() orelse return error.BadFormat;
    if (!std.mem.eql(u8, header, "smallledger 1")) return error.BadFormat;

    while (lines.next()) |line| {
        if (line.len == 0) continue;
        var it = std.mem.tokenizeScalar(u8, line, ' ');
        const kind = it.next() orelse continue;
        if (std.mem.eql(u8, kind, "seed")) {
            co.seed = try num(u64, &it);
            co.rng = Rng.init(co.seed);
        } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, kind, "clock")) {
            co.clock.day_index = try num(u32, &it);
            co.clock.date = .{ .year = try num(u16, &it), .month = try num(u8, &it), .day = try num(u8, &it) };
        } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, kind, "funds")) {
            co.funds = try num(CBills, &it);
            co.starting_funds = try num(CBills, &it);
            co.next_id = try num(u32, &it);
        } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, kind, "rng")) {
            const i = try num(usize, &it);
            if (i >= Stream.count) return error.BadFormat;
            for (&co.rng.prngs[i].s) |*s| s.* = try num(u64, &it);
        } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, kind, "person")) {
            const id = try num(u32, &it);
            const name = it.next() orelse return error.BadFormat;
            const role = std.meta.stringToEnum(Role, it.next() orelse return error.BadFormat) orelse return error.BadFormat;
            const hired_day = try num(u32, &it);
            const morale = try num(i8, &it);
            try co.people.append(co.allocator(), .{
                .id = @enumFromInt(id),
                .name = try co.allocator().dupe(u8, name),
                .role = role,
                .hired_day = hired_day,
                .morale = morale,
            });
        } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, kind, "txn")) {
            const day = try num(u32, &it);
            const amount = try num(CBills, &it);
            const cat = std.meta.stringToEnum(Category, it.next() orelse return error.BadFormat) orelse return error.BadFormat;
            const note = try co.allocator().dupe(u8, it.rest());
            try co.ledger.post(co.allocator(), .{ .day = day, .amount = amount, .category = cat, .note = note });
        } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, kind, "log")) {
            try co.log.append(co.allocator(), try co.allocator().dupe(u8, it.rest()));
        } else {
            return error.BadFormat;
        }
    }
    return co;
}

fn num(comptime T: type, it: *std.mem.TokenIterator(u8, .scalar)) LoadError!T {
    const tok = it.next() orelse return error.BadFormat;
    return std.fmt.parseInt(T, tok, 10) catch error.BadFormat;
}

pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void {
    const io = init.io;
    const gpa = init.gpa;
    var out_buf: [4096]u8 = undefined;
    var stdout = std.Io.File.stdout().writer(io, &out_buf);
    const out = &stdout.interface;
    var in_buf: [1024]u8 = undefined;
    var stdin = std.Io.File.stdin().reader(io, &in_buf);

    var co = Company.init(gpa, .{});
    defer co.deinit();

    while (true) {
        try out.flush();
        const raw = try stdin.interface.takeDelimiter('\n') orelse break;
        const line = std.mem.trim(u8, raw, " \t\r\n");
        if (line.len == 0) continue;
        const cmd = parseLine(line) catch |e| {
            try out.print("> error: {s}\n", .{@errorName(e)});
            continue;
        };
        switch (cmd) {
            .sim => |c| {
                const result = execute(&co, c) catch |e| {
                    try out.print("> error: {s}\n", .{@errorName(e)});
                    continue;
                };
                switch (result) {
                    .hired => |id| try out.print("> hired {s} as {s} (id {d})\n", .{ c.hire.name, @tagName(c.hire.role), @intFromEnum(id) }),
                    .fired => try out.print("> fired {d}\n", .{@intFromEnum(c.fire)}),
                    .advanced => |n| try out.print("> advanced {d} days to {d}-{d:0>2}-{d:0>2}, funds {d}\n", .{
                        n, co.clock.date.year, co.clock.date.month, co.clock.date.day, co.funds,
                    }),
                }
            },
            .people => {
                for (co.people.items) |p| {
                    try out.print("> {d:>3}  {s:<10} {s:<10} morale {d:>3}  pay {d}\n", .{
                        @intFromEnum(p.id), p.name, @tagName(p.role), p.morale, p.monthlySalary(),
                    });
                }
                if (co.people.items.len == 0) try out.print("> nobody on the roster\n", .{});
            },
            .ledger => {
                for (co.ledger.transactions.items) |t| {
                    try out.print("> day {d}  {d}  {s}  {s}\n", .{ t.day, t.amount, @tagName(t.category), t.note });
                }
                try out.print("balance {d}\n", .{co.funds});
            },
            .log => {
                for (co.log.items) |l| try out.print("> {s}\n", .{l});
                if (co.log.items.len == 0) try out.print("> quiet so far\n", .{});
            },
            .save => |path| {
                save(io, &co, path) catch |e| {
                    try out.print("> save failed: {s}\n", .{@errorName(e)});
                    continue;
                };
                try out.print("> saved {s}\n", .{path});
            },
            .load => |path| {
                const loaded = load(io, gpa, path) catch |e| {
                    try out.print("> load failed: {s}\n", .{@errorName(e)});
                    continue;
                };
                co.deinit();
                co = loaded;
                try out.print("> loaded {s}: day {d}, {d} people, funds {d}\n", .{ path, co.clock.day_index, co.people.items.len, co.funds });
            },
            .quit => break,
        }
    }
    try out.print("> bye\n", .{});
    try out.flush();
}

test "save then load reproduces the hash" {
    const io = std.testing.io;
    const gpa = std.testing.allocator;
    var co = Company.init(gpa, .{ .seed = 9 });
    defer co.deinit();
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .hire = .{ .name = "Grayson", .role = .mekwarrior } });
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .advance_days = 60 });
    try save(io, &co, "test_roundtrip.sav");
    defer std.Io.Dir.cwd().deleteFile(io, "test_roundtrip.sav") catch {};
    var back = try load(io, gpa, "test_roundtrip.sav");
    defer back.deinit();
    try std.testing.expectEqual(co.hash(), back.hash());
    // and the two continue identically, because the RNG state was saved
    _ = try execute(&co, .{ .advance_days = 100 });
    _ = try execute(&back, .{ .advance_days = 100 });
    try std.testing.expectEqual(co.hash(), back.hash());
}

test "parseLine" {
    const c = try parseLine("hire Grayson mekwarrior");
    try std.testing.expectEqualStrings("Grayson", c.sim.hire.name);
    try std.testing.expectError(error.BadRole, parseLine("hire X pirate"));
    try std.testing.expectError(error.UnknownVerb, parseLine("dance"));
    try std.testing.expectError(error.BadNumber, parseLine("advance ten"));
}
$ zig test ex6_repl.zig
All 2 tests passed.
$ printf 'load ledger.sav\npeople\nadvance 300\nlog\nfire 2\npeople\nbogus\n' | zig run ex6_repl.zig

> day 142: a good day (rolled 12), morale +1
> day 163: a good day (rolled 12), morale +1

> day 295: a good day (rolled 12), morale +1
